Read the figure and answer the question. <image1> In the process of Earth revolving from position A to position B, how many degrees of latitude has the direct solar point moved through?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there are two positions on Earth's orbit around the Sun, the lower left is labeled “A,” and the upper right is labeled “B”; the question stem states that A and B represent an equinox point and a solstice point, and Earth's direction of motion is from A to B. Then reason: at an equinox, the Sun directly shines on the equator, and the latitude of the direct solar point is 0°; at a solstice, the Sun directly shines on the Tropic of Capricorn or the Tropic of Cancer, and the latitude of the direct solar point is 23°26′. Therefore, from an equinox point to a solstice point, the number of degrees of latitude through which the direct solar point moves is |23°26′－0°|=23°26′.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify 甲 and 乙 as the two given positions on Earth’s orbit, one being a 分点 and the other a 至点. From the text, the motion is from 甲 to 乙. Assign the subsolar latitude at the equinox as 0° and at the solstice as 23°26′ on the relevant side of the equator. Compute the latitude span crossed by the subsolar point: |23°26′ − 0°| = 23°26′.
